summary: Global Capacity Alliance moves to intervene and comments on the June 18 show cause orders, proposing Front-of-the-Meter Netting and a Capacity Attribution Contract so flexible large loads can pair with co-located resources while upgrades are built.
ask: Grant intervention and direct the RTOs and ISOs, in responding to the show cause orders, to evaluate Front-of-the-Meter Netting frameworks and independent standard-setting pathways.

points.point: GCA says a separately metered load and battery at one substation can be curtailed and dispatched at once because dispatch has no link between them.
points.quote: A 100 MW data center and a 100 MW BESS sit at the same substation on separate meters.

points.point: FTM-Netting rests on a telemetry shield, a post-operating-day compliance ledger and scarcity yielding in system-wide emergencies.
points.quote: Telemetry Shield: Each dispatch interval, the Market Participant (MP) dynamically adjusts the load's consumption floor via market telemetry to match the paired resource's availability

points.point: A private Capacity Attribution Contract bridges non-firm energization and completed network upgrades, then sunsets when the load turns firm.
points.quote: its commercial engine is the private Capacity Attribution Contract (CAC), which bridges the gap between initial non-firm energization and completed network upgrades.

points.point: Because the assets are separately metered they stay visible in planning models, unlike behind-the-meter setups.
points.quote: they are studied as standard, independent interconnections—fully visible to RTO planning models and subject to existing constraint analyses.

points.point: GCA asks FERC to direct RTO and ISO responses to evaluate FTM-Netting.
points.quote: urges the Commission to direct the RTOs and ISOs, in responding to the June 18, 2026, Show Cause Orders, to actively evaluate and incorporate Front-of-the-Meter (FTM) Netting frameworks

throughLine.text: Comment filed across the show cause dockets; its netting and interim non-firm service concept speaks to the flexible-load service and co-location topics the June orders direct RTOs to address.
